message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long‑weekend holidays that Canadians can expect in 2023**.  
(“Long weekend” means the holiday falls on a Friday or Monday, or is observed on the nearest weekday, giving you a three‑day break.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if applicable) | Typical long‑weekend span |
|---------|-------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Sunday Jan 1 | Observed Monday Jan 2 | Dec 30–Jan 2 (or Jan 1–3) |
| **Family Day** *(Alberta, BC, NB, ON, SK)* | Monday Feb 20 | — | Feb 18–20 |
| **Good Friday** | Friday Apr 7 | — | Apr 7–9 |
| **Victoria Day** | Monday May 22 | — | May 20–22 |
| **Canada Day** | Saturday Jul 1 | Observed Monday Jul 3 | Jul 1–3 |
| **Labour Day** | Monday Sep 4 | — | Sep 2–4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Monday Oct 9 | — | Oct 7–9 |
| **Remembrance Day** | Monday Nov 11 | — | Nov 9–11 |
| **Christmas Day** | Monday Dec 25 | — | Dec 23–25 |
| **Boxing Day** | Tuesday Dec 26 | Observed Monday Dec 26 (if Dec 26 is a holiday) | Dec 24–26 |

### Notes

1. **Provincial Variations** – Some holidays (e.g., Family Day, Civic Holiday, etc.) are province‑specific. The table above lists only the federal holidays that create long weekends nationwide.  
2. **Observed Dates** – When a holiday falls on a weekend, Canada usually observes it on the nearest weekday (often the following Monday).  
3. **Extended Breaks** – If you’re planning a getaway, consider the weekend that borders the holiday (e.g., the Friday before Good Friday or the Saturday after Canada Day) to maximize your time off.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app or use the dates as a starting point for scheduling trips!
